Clustering statistics for an increasing number of clusters

Source: R/cstats_table.R
cstats_table.Rd

Cuts the clustering tree into step, 2 * step, ..., k clusters and computes, for each number of clusters, the statistics of fpc::cluster.stats(). The average silhouette width can be plotted to help choosing the number of clusters.

Usage

cstats_table(dist, tree, k, step, graph_silhouette = TRUE, l)

Source

Adapted from the cstats.table() function and the silhouette plot of Anastasia Reusova's tutorial: Reusova A. (2018). Hierarchical Clustering on Categorical Data in R. Towards Data Science. https://medium.com/@anastasia.reusova/hierarchical-clustering-on-categorical-data-in-r-a27e578f2995. Code: https://github.com/khunreus/cluster-categorical.

Arguments

dist

A dissimilarity object, e.g. gower_dist returned by assess_gower().

tree

An hclust object, e.g. aggl.clust.c returned by assess_gower().

k

Largest number of clusters to test. Must be a multiple of step.

step

Increment between two numbers of clusters tested.

graph_silhouette

If TRUE (default), the average silhouette width is plotted against the number of clusters.

l

Deprecated, use step instead.

Value

A data frame with one row per number of clusters tested (row names Test <number of clusters>) and the columns cluster.number, n, within.cluster.ss, average.within, average.between, wb.ratio, dunn2, avg.silwidth (see fpc::cluster.stats()), followed by cluster size columns. Values are rounded to 2 decimals.

See also

Other clustering method: assess_gower(), select_silhouette()

Examples

datafile <- system.file("data_test.csv", package = "strainselect")
raw_data <- read.csv(datafile, sep = ";", header = TRUE)
prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c(7, 10, 13, 14, 17, 24),
                               id = 1, date = 17)
#> no duplicate ID
#> selected metadata: CONTEXTE, MATRICE1, REGION, SECTEUR, LIEUPVT, ANNEE
gower <- assess_gower(prepared_data, graph = FALSE)
stats <- cstats_table(dist = gower$gower_dist, tree = gower$aggl.clust.c,
                      k = 50, step = 10)
#> testing 10 clusters
#> testing 20 clusters
#> testing 30 clusters
#> testing 40 clusters
#> testing 50 clusters

stats[, c("cluster.number", "avg.silwidth")]
#>         cluster.number avg.silwidth
#> Test 10             10         0.29
#> Test 20             20         0.41
#> Test 30             30         0.39
#> Test 40             40         0.49
#> Test 50             50         0.48
